title: Request Validation at the API Boundary
summary: Quick revision notes on validating input at the edge of an API: schemas, 400 vs 422, consistent error bodies, field-level errors, sanitization and size limits.

chapters.title: The Boundary Mental Model
points: Boundary validation: check every byte from outside (body, query, path, headers, cookies, uploads) once, at the edge, before business logic runs
Parse, don't validate: turn raw input into a typed object; code past the boundary only sees valid data and never re-checks it
Layers: syntax (JSON parses) → schema (types, required, formats) → semantics (business rules such as end date after start date) → authorization; fail at the earliest layer
Client-side checks are only UX; the server must validate everything because requests can bypass the UI with curl or scripts

Interview Point: Why validate at the boundary rather than deep in services? What is 'parse, don't validate'? Why is client-side validation never enough? Which checks belong in the schema and which in business logic?

chapters.title: Schemas: Declarative Validation
points: A schema declares the contract once (type, required, min/max, regex, enum, nested objects) and a library enforces it (Pydantic, Zod, Joi, JSON Schema, Bean Validation)
Reject unknown fields (strict or additionalProperties:false) to catch typos and mass-assignment; allowlist fields, never blocklist
Separate input schemas from DB models: a CreateUser schema has no id or role, so clients cannot set them (mass-assignment/overposting)
Example: z.object({ email: z.string().email(), age: z.number().int().min(18) }).strict().safeParse(body) returns success or a list of issues

Interview Point: Why use a schema instead of hand-written if-checks? What is mass assignment and how do schemas prevent it? Strict vs lenient handling of unknown fields? Where should coercion happen (e.g. '5' to 5)?

chapters.title: 400 vs 422 and Status Codes
points: 400 Bad Request: the request is malformed and cannot be understood (broken JSON, wrong Content-Type framing, bad query syntax)
422 Unprocessable Content: syntax is valid and the server understood it, but the values fail semantic or schema rules (email format, negative quantity)
Comparison: invalid JSON → 400; valid JSON with age:-1 → 422; FastAPI uses 422 for schema errors, many APIs (Spring, Express) use 400 for both. Pick one convention and document it
Related codes: 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 missing resource, 409 state conflict (duplicate email), 413 body too large, 415 unsupported media type, 429 rate limited
Interview Point: 400 vs 422, what is the difference? When is 409 correct instead? Which code for an oversized body or wrong Content-Type? Should validation failures ever return 200 or 500?

chapters.title: Consistent Error Bodies and Field-Level Errors
points: Every error uses one envelope, e.g. RFC 9457 Problem Details: { type, title, status, detail, instance } with Content-Type application/problem+json
Field-level errors: return an errors array of { field: 'address.zip', code: 'invalid_format', message: '...' } so clients can highlight each input
Report all field errors in one response, not just the first, so users fix everything in one round trip
Use stable machine-readable codes (too_short, required) plus a human message; clients branch on code, never on message text

Interview Point: Why a single error format across all endpoints? What does RFC 9457 define? Should you return all errors or only the first? How do you represent nested or array field paths? What must never appear in an error body?

chapters.title: Sanitization and Size Limits
points: Validation rejects bad input; sanitization changes it (trim, normalize Unicode, strip control characters). Prefer rejecting over silently altering
Sanitize by output context, not on input: parameterized queries for SQL, HTML-escape on render, no shell string concatenation. Input cleaning alone does not stop injection
Limit sizes at every level: body bytes (413), string max length, array length, nesting depth, upload size; enforce at the proxy or server before the body is fully read
Also bound pagination (max limit=100), number ranges, regex complexity (ReDoS), and decompressed size (zip bombs)

Interview Point: Validation vs sanitization, what is the difference? Why escape on output rather than input? Where do you enforce body size limits and which status code? How can missing limits cause a DoS?

chapters.title: Validation Cheat Sheet
points: Order: parse → schema → authz → business rules, because a state check such as a duplicate must not answer a caller who lacks permission; validate everything from outside once at the edge and trust typed data afterward
Codes: 400 malformed, 422 semantically invalid, 409 conflict, 413 too large, 415 wrong media type, 429 rate limited
Error body: Problem Details (type, title, status, detail) plus errors[{ field, code, message }], same shape everywhere, all errors at once
Schemas: allowlist fields, strict unknown-key rejection, separate input and DB models, no client-set id or role
Interview Point: Walk through the full path of a bad POST from raw bytes to the error response. What limits and codes apply at each step? How do you keep error shapes consistent across services?
